subject: Annotating genomic coordinates with genes and distance from genes

messages.author: 67571e909b2d8a9a
messages.subject: Annotating genomic coordinates with genes and distance from genes
parts:
Hi,

Could I please be advised on how I might be able to annotate my list of differentially methylated cytosines (DMCs) with genes and the distance they are from the transcriptional start site.

I understand that MethylKit has the following command to generate a list of genes associated with the DMCs and distance from the transcriptional start site:

annotate.WithGenicParts(myDiff25p,gene.obj)

However, the list generated from this command does not link the annotation information to the coordinates of the DMCs. Is there a way that I might be able to link the output of this command to the coordinates of my DMCs?

Thanks,

Ben

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Annotating genomic coordinates with genes and distance from genes
parts:
Hi,
it shouldn't be sorted differently.it keeps the order from "target" at annotate.WithGenicParts(target,GRangesList.obj,strand=FALSE)

so cbind( getData(target)[x$target.row,], x) should get you what you want. x being the result of getAssociationWithTSS()

Best,
Altuna

messages.author: 23a2cb256755f4e1
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Annotating genomic coordinates with genes and distance from genes
parts:
Dear Altuna
Same as Jason Liao I'm concern when I annotate differentially methylated CpGs  in this way (assign a gene name by the distance to the nearest TSS). We usually annotate CpGs with gene names to prepare the data set for further analysis (i.e. gene ontology). And we usually assume that the differential methylation is some how affecting that gene (the one we linked to the DM-CpG). However there are plenty of evidence that methylation in promoters  and methylation in exons  have different consequences in the activity of a gene.
It is any way to annotate DM-CpG following a precedence rule ( one that give exons priority during the annotation)?
Txs.
Ale

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Annotating genomic coordinates with genes and distance from genes
parts:
There might be cases where distance to nearest TSS is shorter to the TSS of adjacent gene for an exonic DMC.

You get an annotation matrix see getMembers() function. That matrix contains the TRUE/FALSE or (0/1) values for a DMC overlapping with promoter/exon/intron. you can come up with your own precedence rule using that matrix.

Best,
Altuna

parts:
Dear Dr Altuna,

Good day to you. I'm facing same problem (the annotation list is sorted differently) and would like to try on command as per suggested: cbind( getData(target)[x$target.row,], x) --> but fail to do so as I'm not sure the correct object to fill in target and x in the command. 

My previous command is shown as below: 
library(genomation) ; gene.obj=readTranscriptFeatures("2018_all_refseq.rn6.bed.txt") ; 
diffAnn.all=annotateWithGeneParts(as(myDiff25p.all,"GRanges"),gene.obj) ; 
dput(diffAnn.all,"1_F0CvsF1C_diffAnn_all.txt") ; 
tss.assoc.all <- getAssociationWithTSS (diffAnn.all) ; 

Kindly please help, thanks Dr Altuna.
On Monday, August 11, 2014 at 4:25:25 AM UTC+8, Altuna Akalin wrote:

Hi,
it shouldn't be sorted differently.it keeps the order from "target" at annotate.WithGenicParts(target,GRangesList.obj,strand=FALSE)

so cbind( getData(target)[x$target.row,], x) should get you what you want. x being the result of getAssociationWithTSS()

Best,
Altuna
